examples.en: I wrote my name in big letters on my bag with a marker.
Marker writing doesn't come off easily.
Make sure to keep the marker's cap closed.
The child scribbled on the wall with a marker.
Please lend me just one black marker.
The marker smells a bit.

explain: 글씨가 잘 지워지지 않아서 이름을 쓰거나 큰 글씨를 쓸 때 써요. 같은 종류를 '네임펜'이라고도 해요. '사인펜'은 따로 있는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I wrote my name with a permanent marker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매직펜과 같은 종류를 부르는 다른 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the same kind of pen as 매직펜.

phrases.en: Please write it big with a marker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 펜 이름 뒤에 '(으)로'를 붙여 도구를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add (으)로 after the pen name to show the tool.

phrases.en: Please give me one black marker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색깔을 앞에 붙여서 필요한 펜을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the color before it to say which marker you need.

explain_en: Its writing doesn't come off easily, so it is used for writing names or large letters. The same kind of pen is also called '네임펜'. '사인펜' is a different word for a different kind of pen.

examples.en: I filled the water glass to the brim.
I broke a glass and cut my hand a little.

examples.ko: 아침 물 한 잔을 위해 머리맡에 물컵을 올려 뒀어요.
examples.en: For my morning glass of water, I put a cup by my bed.
This glass is made of glass, so you have to be careful.
Please bring two water glasses.
When I do the dishes, I wash the water glasses first.

explain: '컵'은 종이컵, 머그컵처럼 종류가 많아서 물 마시는 용도를 분명히 할 때 '물컵'이라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '물잔'도 있어요. 물은 '따르다'와 함께 써서 '물컵에 물을 따르다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I put ice in the water glass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물컵과 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word similar to 물컵.

phrases.en: I washed the water glass while doing the dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설거지할 때 '씻다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 씻다 (to wash) when doing dishes.

phrases.en: Please give me one more water glass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이나 집에서 컵을 더 달라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask for one more glass at a restaurant or home.

explain_en: '컵' covers many kinds, such as paper cups and mugs, so '물컵' makes clear it is for drinking water. '물잔' is a similar word. It goes with '따르다', as in '물컵에 물을 따르다'.

examples.en: Please put the fruit in a plastic bag.

examples.ko: 비닐봉지 값을 따로 받은 뒤로 장바구니를 들고 오는 손님이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Since they started charging for plastic bags, more customers bring shopping bags.
The plastic bag tore and the things spilled out.

examples.ko: 일회용 비닐봉지는 돈을 내고 사야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay for single-use plastic bags.
Could you give me one more plastic bag?
I took a shopping bag instead of a plastic bag.

explain: 줄여서 그냥 '봉지'나 '비닐'이라고도 말해요. 종이로 만든 '종이봉투'와 짝으로 생각하면 편해요. 마트에서 '봉지 필요하세요?'라고 자주 물어봐요.

phrases.en: Shall I put it in a bag for you?
phrases.nuance_ko: '비닐봉지'를 줄여 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened way to say 비닐봉지.

phrases.en: I got a plastic bag at the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 물건을 담을 봉지를 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting a bag for goods at a store.

phrases.en: Please use a paper bag instead of a plastic bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이로 만든 봉투로, 비닐봉지와 짝으로 생각하면 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bag made of paper; easy to remember as the pair of 비닐봉지.

explain_en: People often shorten it to just '봉지' or '비닐'. It helps to think of it as the counterpart of '종이봉투' (paper bag). At supermarkets you often hear '봉지 필요하세요?'.

examples.en: The shop's glass door says 'Please pull'.

examples.ko: 유리문을 밀고 들어가니 시원한 바람이 불었어요.
examples.en: When I pushed open the glass door, a cool breeze blew.
A bird hit the glass door and I was startled.

examples.ko: 유리문 너머로 아이들이 노는 모습이 보여요.
examples.en: I can see the children playing beyond the glass door.
Close the glass door carefully so it doesn't break.
The whole front of this shop is glass doors.

explain: '유리창'은 열어서 바깥을 보는 창이고 '유리문'은 열고 드나드는 문이에요. 가게 입구나 베란다 문을 말할 때 자주 써요. '유리문을 밀다/당기다/열다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I opened the glass door and went into the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문으로 드나들 때 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for going through a door.

phrases.en: It's cold, so please close the glass door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁할 때 '-아 주세요'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-a juseyo' when making a request.

phrases.en: I'll wait in front of the glass door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만날 장소를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to set a meeting place.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the glass door

explain_en: '유리창' is a window you look out of, while '유리문' is a door you go in and out through. It's often used for shop entrances or balcony doors. It goes with verbs like '밀다' (push), '당기다' (pull), and '열다' (open).

examples.ko: 이력서에 붙일 증명사진을 찍으러 사진관에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a photo studio to get an ID photo for my résumé.

examples.ko: 증명사진이 마음에 안 들어서 다시 찍었어요.
examples.en: I didn't like my ID photo, so I had it taken again.
ID photos for passports have a set size.
There are two ID photos in my wallet.
Do you need just one more ID photo?

examples.ko: 사진관에서 증명사진을 찍는 데 만 원 들었어요.
examples.en: It cost ten thousand won to get an ID photo at the studio.

explain: 여권, 이력서, 신분증 같은 서류에 쓰는 얼굴 사진이에요. '증명사진을 찍다', '증명사진을 붙이다'처럼 써요. 그냥 '사진'이라고 하면 일상 사진도 되니까 서류용일 때 '증명사진'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I had an ID photo taken for my passport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류에 쓸 사진을 새로 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting a new photo for documents.

phrases.en: Please attach an ID photo to the form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류를 낼 때 사진을 붙이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when telling someone to attach a photo to a form.

phrases.en: What size should the ID photo be?
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류마다 사진 크기가 달라서 자주 묻는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common question since photo sizes differ by document.

explain_en: It's a face photo for documents such as passports, résumés, and ID cards. Say '증명사진을 찍다' (take) and '증명사진을 붙이다' (attach). Plain '사진' can be any photo, so use '증명사진' when you mean one for documents.

examples.en: In the morning I toast bread in the toaster.
The finished bread popped out of the toaster.

examples.ko: 저는 매일 토스터로 빵을 구워 먹어요.
examples.en: I toast bread with a toaster every day.

examples.ko: 토스터가 고장 나서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The toaster broke, so I need to buy a new one.

examples.ko: 작은 토스터라서 한 번에 두 장만 구울 수 있어요.
examples.en: It is a small toaster, so it can only toast two slices at a time.

examples.ko: 이 토스터는 빵이 잘 타지 않아요.
examples.en: Bread doesn't burn easily in this toaster.

explain: 기계는 '토스터', 구운 빵으로 만든 음식은 '토스트'로 달라요. 빵은 '토스터에 굽다'처럼 '굽다'와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: If you toast bread in a toaster, it gets crispy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빵을 기계로 구울 때 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing for toasting bread with the machine.

phrases.en: I put two slices of bread in the toaster.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굽기 전에 빵을 넣는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes putting bread in before toasting.
phrases.en_equiv: to put bread in the toaster

phrases.en: I bought a new toaster.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 새로 살 때 쓰는 짧은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short phrase for buying a new one.

explain_en: The machine is a '토스터', while the food made from toasted bread is '토스트'. Bread goes with '굽다', as in '토스터에 굽다'.

examples.ko: 내일 아침 여섯 시에 모닝콜 부탁드려요.
examples.en: Please give me a wake-up call at six tomorrow morning.
I got a wake-up call at the hotel and barely got up.

examples.ko: 알람이 안 들려서 친구한테 모닝콜을 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't hear my alarm, so I asked a friend for a wake-up call.

examples.ko: 모닝콜이 울려도 저는 또 잠들어 버렸어요.
examples.en: Even when the wake-up call rang, I fell asleep again.
Is the wake-up call service free at this hotel?

examples.ko: 남편이 매일 아침 일곱 시에 모닝콜을 해 줘요.
examples.en: My husband gives me a wake-up call every morning at seven.

explain: 호텔에서는 '모닝콜 서비스'라고 많이 말해요. 친구나 가족이 전화로 깨워 줄 때도 '모닝콜 해 줘'라고 말해요. 휴대폰에서 울리는 소리는 보통 '알람'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: This hotel has a wake-up call service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호텔에서 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase commonly used at hotels.

phrases.example: 내일 아침에 모닝콜 좀 해 줘요.
phrases.en: Please give me a wake-up call tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족에게 깨워 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask a friend or family member to wake you up.

phrases.en: I set the alarm for seven o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰에서 울리는 소리는 모닝콜이 아니라 알람이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sound from a phone is called an alarm, not a morning call.

explain_en: At hotels you often hear '모닝콜 서비스'. When a friend or family member phones to wake you, you can say '모닝콜 해 줘'. The sound your phone makes is usually called '알람'.

examples.en: I make two copies of each contract.
I made a copy of my passport to give to the company.
You must not copy this book.
How much per page does it cost to make a copy?
I copied the file and put it on a USB drive.
I pasted the copied text into the email.

explain: 복사기로 종이를 복사하는 것도, 컴퓨터에서 복사해서 붙이는 것도 '복사하다'예요. 컴퓨터에서는 '복사하다'와 '붙여넣다'를 짝으로 써요. 남의 숙제를 그대로 따라 쓰는 건 '복사'가 아니라 '베끼다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I copy this text and paste it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터에서 복사와 붙여넣기를 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for copying and pasting on a computer in one phrase.

phrases.example: 이 서류를 두 장 복사해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please make two copies of this document.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 복사를 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to make a copy.

phrases.en: I copied the book yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 복사한 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for something already copied.

explain_en: Photocopying paper and copy-pasting on a computer are both 복사하다. On a computer it pairs with '붙여넣다' (paste). Copying someone else's homework word for word is '베끼다', not 복사.

examples.ko: 여름에는 해수욕장마다 파라솔과 튜브를 빌려주는 가게가 생겨요.
examples.en: In summer, shops that rent out parasols and tubes appear at every beach.

examples.ko: 친구가 비 오는 날 우산을 빌려줬어요.
examples.en: My friend lent me an umbrella on a rainy day.
It's heavy, so could you lend me a hand?
It's hard to lend money even to a close friend.

examples.ko: 제 노트를 빌려줄 테니까 복사해서 쓰세요.
examples.en: I'll lend you my notes, so copy them and use them.

examples.ko: 도서관에서는 책을 이 주 동안 빌려줘요.
examples.en: The library lends books for two weeks.

explain: '빌리다'는 받는 쪽, '빌려주다'는 주는 쪽이에요. 윗사람에게 줄 때는 '빌려 드리다'라고 해요. 돈이나 물건을 빌려주고 받는 일은 '빌리다-빌려주다'를 짝으로 기억하면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: My friends lent a hand on moving day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 손을 주는 게 아니라 일을 도와준다는 뜻이에요. 부탁할 때는 '손 좀 빌려주세요'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: No hand is actually lent; it means helping with a task. When asking, you say '손 좀 빌려주세요'.

explain_en: '빌리다' is the borrowing side and '빌려주다' is the lending side. When the receiver is older or senior, say '빌려 드리다'. It helps to remember the pair '빌리다-빌려주다'.

examples.en: The front door of the shop is locked, so please come to the back door.

examples.ko: 택배 기사님이 앞문 앞에 상자를 두고 가셨어요.
examples.en: The delivery driver left the box in front of the front door.
The front door was broken, so I went in through the back door.

examples.ko: 수업이 시작되자 교실 앞문으로 선생님이 들어오셨어요.
examples.en: When class began, the teacher came in through the front door of the classroom.
A seat near the front door on the subway is empty.

examples.ko: 차 앞문을 열고 아이를 먼저 태웠어요.
examples.en: I opened the front door of the car and put the child in first.

explain: 반대말은 '뒷문'이고, 교실이나 버스처럼 앞뒤에 문이 있는 곳에서 많이 써요. 학교나 건물의 '정문'은 정식 출입구를 가리켜서 '앞문'과 항상 같지는 않아요. '앞문으로 들어가다, 앞문으로 나가다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Please get on the bus through the front door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어가는 문을 말할 때 '으로'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 'euro' to say which door you enter through.
phrases.en_equiv: to enter through the front door

phrases.en: If you go out the classroom's front door, it's the hallway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나가는 문을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which door you exit through.
phrases.en_equiv: to exit through the front door

phrases.en: Our classroom has a front door and a back door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '뒷문'과 함께 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with its opposite 'dwitmun' (back door).

explain_en: Its opposite is '뒷문' (back door), and it is common in places with doors at both ends, like classrooms and buses. A school or building's '정문' (main gate) is the official entrance and is not always the same as the '앞문'. You say '앞문으로 들어가다/나가다' (go in/out through the front door).

examples.en: The child sharpened the pencil to a point with a pencil sharpener.
The pencil sharpener broke, so I sharpened it with a knife.
I put a small pencil sharpener on the desk.

examples.ko: 시험 전날 연필깎이 앞에서 연필을 깎았어요.
examples.en: The day before the exam, I sharpened pencils at the sharpener.
The pencil sharpener is full of pencil shavings.
I bought a portable pencil sharpener at the stationery store.

explain: 발음은 [연필까끼]예요. '연필을 깎다'에서 나온 말이라서 도구를 나타내는 '-이'가 붙었어요. 칼로 깎을 때는 '연필을 깎다'라고만 해요.

phrases.en: I sharpened the pencil with a pencil sharpener.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 나타내는 '(으)로'와 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase, with 'euro' marking the tool.

phrases.en: There is a small pencil sharpener in my pencil case.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 꾸며 물건을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the size of the object.

phrases.en: I bought a pencil sharpener at the stationery store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 사는 상황에서 간단히 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple phrase for a shopping situation.

explain_en: It is pronounced [연필까끼]. It comes from '연필을 깎다' (sharpen a pencil), with '-이' added to name the tool. If you do it with a knife, you simply say '연필을 깎다'.

examples.ko: 문자로 온 인증 코드를 입력해 주세요.
examples.en: Please enter the verification code that came by text.

examples.ko: 개발자는 하루 종일 컴퓨터로 코드를 써요.
examples.en: Developers write code on the computer all day.

examples.ko: 어느 코드가 맞는지 다시 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Please check again which code is correct.
Today's dress code for the gathering is black.
The price goes down if you just enter the discount code.

examples.ko: 이 코드를 복사해서 아래에 붙여 넣어요.
examples.en: Copy this code and paste it below.

explain: '인증 코드', '할인 코드', '드레스 코드'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여서 많이 써요. 프로그램을 쓴 글도 '코드'라고 해요. 비슷한 '번호'는 숫자만 있을 때, '코드'는 글자와 숫자가 섞일 때도 써요. 사람 사이에서 쓰는 '코드가 맞다'도 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 저는 그 친구랑 코드가 잘 맞아요.
phrases.en: to click with someone; be on the same wavelength
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람끼리 취향이나 성격, 말투가 잘 맞을 때 말해요. 친구나 동료 사이에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two people's tastes, personalities, or way of talking fit well. It is casual, used among friends and coworkers.

explain_en: It is used with a word in front, as in 인증 코드, 할인 코드, and 드레스 코드. Programming text is also called 코드. 번호 fits when there are only digits, while 코드 can mix letters and numbers. It is also worth knowing the phrase 코드가 맞다, used between people.

examples.en: The child drew a picture on the wallpaper with crayons.

examples.ko: 동생이 벽에 선을 그어서 크레파스를 뺏겼어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling drew lines on the wall and had the crayons taken away.
The crayon broke, so I bought a new one.
I put a twelve-color crayon set in my bag.
When I was little, I liked the smell of crayons.
Could you lend me your crayons?

explain: 연필처럼 깎아서 쓰는 '색연필'과 달리, 크레파스는 문질러서 넓게 칠하는 그림 도구예요. 주로 어린이 미술 시간에 쓰는 물건이라 '크레파스로 칠하다/그리다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The child colored the sky with crayons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓은 곳에 색을 채울 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits well when filling a wide area with color.

phrases.en: I drew a picture of my family with crayons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림을 그리는 도구를 말할 때 '로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 로 to name the tool used for drawing.

phrases.en: I bought a box of crayons at the stationery store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 색이 든 한 세트를 셀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to count one set with many colors.

explain_en: Unlike colored pencils that you sharpen, a cray-pas is rubbed on to color wide areas. It is mostly an item for children's art class, so you say '크레파스로 칠하다/그리다'.

examples.en: I booked a package tour to Jeju Island this summer.

examples.ko: 선물 패키지가 예뻐서 포장을 버리기 아까워요.
examples.en: The gift package is so pretty that I hate to throw away the wrapping.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 커피와 빵을 패키지로 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop sells coffee and bread as a package.

examples.ko: 패키지 안에 설명서와 충전기가 들어 있어요.
examples.en: The manual and charger come inside the package.
I signed up for Korean lessons at the package price.

examples.ko: 패키지 디자인을 새로 바꿔서 매출이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Sales went up after we changed the package design.

explain: 한국에서는 상품이나 여행을 한데 묶은 것을 '패키지'라고 많이 불러요. 물건을 싸는 일은 '포장'이고, 상품 겉모양은 '패키지'로도 말해요. 택배 상자는 '택배'라고 하고 '패키지'로 부르는 일은 드물어요.

phrases.en: I went on a package tour with my parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교통, 숙소, 관광이 한데 묶인 여행을 말할 때 가장 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use: a trip with transport, lodging and sightseeing bundled together.

phrases.example: 이 호텔은 식사가 들어간 패키지 상품이 있어요.
phrases.en: This hotel has a package deal that includes meals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 가지를 묶어서 파는 상품을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a product sold as a bundle of several things.

phrases.en: The gift package was pretty, so my friend liked it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선물을 담은 겉모양이나 포장 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how a gift is packaged and presented.

explain_en: In Korea 'package' mostly names a bundle of goods or a tour sold together. Wrapping something is '포장', while a product's outer look can also be called its package. A delivery box is called '택배', rarely 'package'.
